judgements.reason: passage covers work, pay, remuneration and trade unions only; slavery and the slave trade are never mentioned
no mention of remedies, tribunals, courts or any enforcement body
no mention of penal offences, guilt, trials or presumption of innocence
no mention of movement, residence, borders or States
'his family' appears only as beneficiary of remuneration; nothing about marriage or consent
no mention of property or of owning anything alone or in association
no mention of social security or of the capacity 'as a member of society', though 'other means of social protection' is adjacent
no mention of rest, leisure, working hours or holidays, though 'just and favourable conditions of work' is adjacent
no mention of any social or international order, nor of realizing the Declaration's rights
no mention of States, groups or persons claiming a right to destroy rights
no mention of arbitrary interference, privacy, home or correspondence
no mention of freedom of movement, residence or State borders
no mention of marriage; 'without any discrimination' attaches to equal pay and lists no grounds such as race, nationality or religion
no mention of government, authority or the will of the people
no mention of rest, leisure, limitation of working hours or paid holidays, though working conditions are discussed
no mention of motherhood, childhood, children or special care and assistance
no mention of duties, the community, or development of personality
no mention of torture or of any treatment or punishment
no mention of hearings, tribunals or equality before a court
no mention of penal offences or of national or international law
no mention of asylum, prosecutions or the United Nations
no mention of nationality or of changing it; only free choice of employment is mentioned
passage grants a right to form and join trade unions but never says anyone may not be compelled to belong to an association
no mention of national effort or international co-operation
no list of situations giving a right to security; only 'protection against unemployment' and 'social protection' are adjacent
no mention of limitations on rights; the word 'just' occurs only in 'just and favourable conditions/remuneration', not as a requirement for limitations
no reference to the Declaration itself or to interpreting it
no list of items protected from arbitrary interference; the word 'arbitrary' does not appear
no mention of asylum, other countries or persecution
no mention of marriage or of consent of spouses
no mention of taking part in government or of representatives
unemployment protection is mentioned but no further circumstances (disability, widowhood, old age) and no 'right to security'
no mention of limitations on the exercise of rights or of how they are determined; 'law' does not appear
no mention of recognition as a person before the law, nor any place such as 'everywhere'
no mention of a hearing, of obligations being determined, or of criminal charges
no mention of penalties or penal offences
no mention of marrying or founding a family, and no enumerated grounds limiting such a right
no mention of property or of deprivation of property; 'arbitrary' does not appear
'existence worthy of human dignity' appears but no enumeration of kinds of rights described as indispensable for dignity
no mention of motherhood, childhood or special care and assistance
